name: Audit remediation
description: Fix, harden, test, refactor and optimize the findings of the 2026-09 codebase audit. Phases are barriers: correctness fixes land before the tests that pin them, refactors before the optimizations that build on them. Parallel steps never own the same files.

phases.name: fixes
phases.description: Verified correctness bugs in agent/, all in untested modules.

steps.name: fix-agent-mcp
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Fix four verified bugs in the agent package's MCP and permission handling. You own ONLY these files: agent/src/mcp.ts, agent/src/tools/index.ts, agent/src/permissions.ts, agent/src/app.ts, agent/src/session.ts. Do not edit other files.

1. MCP tools bypass the permission system: agent/src/tools/index.ts:64 splices session.mcp.tools into the tool set and agent/src/mcp.ts:38 calls client.callTool with no checkPermission, while bash/write_file/edit_file all gate. permissions.ts:4 already declares an 'mcp' PermissionGroup that nothing references. Wrap each MCP tool's execute in the same checkPermission gate the built-in tools use, under the 'mcp' group, honoring sticky always-answers and permission modes (plan mode should refuse like other side-effecting tools).
2. MCP clients and sessions leak: McpHandle.close() (mcp.ts:51) has no caller, and app.ts:46 only ever does sessions.set, never delete. Wire close() into whatever ends or replaces a session (re-session/load of the same id must close the old handle before connecting fresh), and remove replaced sessions from the map.
3. Connect-timeout leaks the transport: at mcp.ts:30, when withTimeout rejects, the client was never pushed to clients, so the spawned stdio child is unreachable. Push before awaiting connect, or close the client in the catch.
4. callTool has no timeout and permission asks are not abortable: give client.callTool a timeout (reuse withTimeout; pick a generous constant, e.g. 10 minutes, since MCP tools can be slow) and wire the session's abort signal into the permission await at permissions.ts:45 so session.cancel() unblocks a pending ask (reject or answer 'cancelled' on abort).

Match the file's existing comment style: comments state constraints, not narration. Verify with: cd agent && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. In your final message, summarize each fix in one sentence and list the files you changed.

steps.name: fix-agent-compaction
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Fix three verified bugs in the agent package's context compaction. You own ONLY: agent/src/compaction.ts, agent/src/turn.ts (the compaction call site around lines 60-100 only — do not restructure the rest of turn.ts, another workstream owns it), agent/src/persistence.ts if strictly needed.

1. Compaction eats the prompt that triggered it: turn.ts:70 pushes the user's message onto session.messages, then turn.ts:81 compacts, and compaction.ts:60 does session.messages = [replacement] — so streamText at turn.ts:98 never sees the message the user just typed, and the JSONL loses it at the compact barrier (persistence.ts:123). Fix so the just-typed user message survives verbatim: either compact before appending it, or exclude it from the summarized slice and re-append it after the replacement. Make sure the persisted JSONL keeps it too.
2. A failed compaction kills the turn: compaction.ts:71 rethrows inside turn.ts's main try. A transient summarizer failure should degrade to running the turn uncompacted (announce the 'failed' compaction_update as it already does, but let the turn proceed), not fail the prompt.
3. Compaction can silently wipe history: compaction.ts:41 has no maxOutputTokens and never checks the summary is non-empty before replacing the whole message array. Add a sane maxOutputTokens and treat an empty/whitespace summary as a failed compaction (which, after fix 2, means the turn proceeds uncompacted).

Match the file's existing comment style. Verify with: cd agent && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize each fix in one sentence and list changed files.

steps.name: fix-agent-tools
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Fix robustness bugs in the agent package's bash and search tools. You own ONLY: agent/src/tools/bash.ts and agent/src/tools/search.ts.

bash.ts:
1. Timeout doesn't kill the process tree: the child at bash.ts:56 is spawned without detached, so kill('SIGKILL') at :97/:104 reaps only bash -c and a backgrounded grandchild survives both the timeout and session cancel. Spawn detached and kill the process group (process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL'), guarding the race where the child already exited).
2. Unbounded delta buffer: bash.ts:91 appends every chunk to pendingDelta with no cap while output is capped at 64KB at :84. Cap pendingDelta the same way (keep the tail, note truncation once).
3. Redundant duplicate timers: bash.ts:97-103 sets two setTimeouts at the same deadline just to record a timedOut flag the kill callback could set itself — collapse to one timer.

search.ts:
4. The synchronous grep fallback at search.ts:191-208 runs a user-supplied regex over every file on the main thread with no deadline — catastrophic backtracking freezes the whole agent process. Add a wall-clock budget checked between files (bail with a truncation note), and give the ripgrep path at :152 a timeout/abort as well.

Match existing comment style. Verify with: cd agent && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize each fix in one sentence and list changed files.

phases.name: hardening
phases.description: Server-side missing timeouts, unbounded buffers and unbounded maps. One step, because the fixes cluster in overlapping files.

steps.name: harden-server
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Harden the server package against hangs and unbounded growth. You own ONLY: server/src/gateway-shim.ts, server/src/workflow-mcp.ts, server/src/quota.ts, server/src/session-list.ts, server/src/routines.ts, server/src/routine-git-trigger.ts.

1. gateway-shim.ts:531 — the proxy fetch to the upstream gateway has no AbortSignal, so a hung upstream pins the request (and its buffered body at :507) forever. Streaming makes a fixed total timeout wrong; add a connect/headers deadline (AbortSignal that is cleared/ignored once headers arrive, or AbortSignal.timeout sized for headers with the body piped after).
2. gateway-shim.ts:420 — loggedNamespaces is a Set keyed sessionId/agentId:namespaces (:516) that only ever grows, purely to dedupe a console.log. Bound it (e.g. cap size with simple eviction, or key by agent only).
3. workflow-mcp.ts:42 — the loopback fetch has no timeout; add AbortSignal.timeout consistent with the tool's wait budget.
4. quota.ts:129,147-158 — run() accumulates child stdout/stderr into strings with no byte ceiling; the only bound is the probe timeout. Follow the existing pattern (git.ts:63 MAX_BUFFER = 8 MiB): cap both streams and stop the child or truncate past the cap.
5. session-list.ts — pages and session counts are capped (:25-26) but raw bytes are not; add a byte ceiling on accumulated listing data.
6. routines.ts:396 deleteRoutine never removes the routine's entry from the fires rate-limit map (:733, pruned only within a window at :794-800); delete it there.
7. routine-git-trigger.ts:187 — the repos cache keyed by project has timestamps but no eviction for projects that stop being watched; evict when a watch is removed.

Match existing comment style — this codebase comments the WHY of a bound, not the mechanics. Verify with: cd server && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize each fix in one sentence and list changed files.

phases.name: tests
phases.description: Pin the fixes phase with tests; every phase-1 bug was in a module no test imported.

steps.name: agent-tests
server-tests
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Close the sharpest server test gaps. You own server/test/** only (plus renames within it); do not modify server/src — if a test reveals a real bug, report it in your final message.

1. server/test/routine-triggers.test.ts is misnamed: it imports only scheduler helpers. Rename it scheduler.test.ts (update any package.json script that names it) and write a real routine-git-trigger test covering server/src/routine-git-trigger.ts — ref parsing (:311) and the debounce window at least; use a temp git repo fixture.
2. server/src/session-socket.ts (replay windowing, caught_up framing) has no direct test, and server/src/index.ts:298-310 warns that logic is version-sensitive. Add tests for SessionJournal.windowStart / the step+byte window budgets and the turn-boundary cut (turnStartAt/earlierPage), including the revive case where the log does not begin with a turn_started — the CLAUDE.md 'Live and replay are one code path' section describes the exact invariants; pin them.
3. The backup route's header-only auth rule (server/routes/misc.ts:113-117 refuses ?token=) is a security invariant with no test; pin it (query token refused, header token accepted).
4. Add direct unit tests for the pure functions in server/src/acp-bridge.ts that currently have none: toWireError (:1158), parseSessionNotification (:119), isModeTwin (:1174).

Follow the existing patterns in server/test/ (the fake agent, connectPair-style helpers). Verify: cd server && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize coverage added and anything found broken.

phases.name: refactor
phases.description: Structural cleanups. Each step owns a disjoint file set; behavior must not change — the suites from the tests phase are the safety net.

steps.name: refactor-server
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Two structural refactors in server/src, no behavior change. You own server/src/sessions.ts, new files you extract from it, server/src/index.ts (onError only), and the six error-class sites listed below.

1. SessionManager (server/src/sessions.ts:414-2033, ~1600 lines) has its seams already drawn as comment banners. Extract, in this order of safety: (a) the stderr ring (:855-895 — pushStderr/stderrSinceMark/enrichError/stderrTail) into its own module; it is fully self-contained. (b) the queue block (:1725-1837, 9 methods) into a SessionQueue collaborator — it talks only to listQueue/startTurn. (c) hostFor (:897, a ~100-line object literal that is really the bridge-callback adapter) into a module beside acp-bridge.ts. Keep the public surface of SessionManager identical; move the banner comments with the code they describe.
2. Error shapes are near-duplicated across six classes (routines.ts:138, workflows.ts:58, boards.ts:84, tasks.ts:39, workspace-fs.ts:44, and fs.ts:28's Object.assign form). Introduce a shared HttpError { status, message } base, make the six extend it, and let index.ts:154's onError read status directly instead of regex-sniffing messages (:158). Keep each class's name and message text so callers and tests are untouched.

Verify: cd server && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize the extraction and list new files.

steps.name: refactor-client-actions
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Refactor the client's actions module, no behavior change. You own client/src/lib/actions.ts and the new modules you extract; you may touch importers only to update import paths.

client/src/lib/actions.ts is 1881 lines returned from a single React.useMemo (:170), which is why none of it is unit-testable. Lift out the parts that are pure REST with no coupling to the socket runtime: the routine/schedule/trigger CRUD block (:1195-1380) and the refreshProjects/McpServers/Skills/Commands/Personas block (:1161-1194) into plain exported functions (taking dispatch or returning data — follow how lib/settings.ts shapes its API calls). Keep the thread-lifecycle core (send, reviveThread, reconnectThread, queue ops) in the hook — it genuinely closes over liveThreads/journalCursors. The useMemo should shrink to the closure-bound core plus thin delegations, so call sites don't churn.

Verify: cd client && pnpm exec tsc -b. Summarize what moved where.

steps.name: refactor-thread-items
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Split a client component file, no behavior change. You own client/src/components/thread-items.tsx, the new client/src/components/workflow-run.tsx, and importers' import lines only.

client/src/components/thread-items.tsx is 1686 lines with two unrelated subjects: lines ~538-1430 are entirely workflow/subagent run rendering (WF_STATE_ICONS, WF_TONE if it lives here, WorkflowStepRow, WorkflowPendingRow, WorkflowPhaseHeading, phasesOf, RunProgress, RunCard/WorkflowRun, RunFactsInline/RunFactsBlock, the run dialog), while the module's export contract is RowView/ThreadItemView (:309, :1446). Move the workflow-run half into client/src/components/workflow-run.tsx, keeping thread-items.tsx importing WorkflowRun for its dispatch. Watch the shared-pane rule in CLAUDE.md: tool-parts.tsx exists so tool-views and thread-items can share primitives without importing each other — the new file must not create an import cycle. Move the rationale comments with the code they describe.

Verify: cd client && pnpm exec tsc -b. Summarize what moved.

steps.name: refactor-local-stores
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Unify the client's device-local stores and fix a real cross-tab bug. You own client/src/lib/pins.ts, view-options.ts, agent-options.ts, keybindings.ts, drafts.ts, boards.ts, tasks-board.ts, notifications-inbox.ts (whichever of these exist), and one new client/src/lib/local-store.ts.

Seven device-local stores each hand-roll read -> module cache -> listeners Set -> write -> useSyncExternalStore. Only pins.ts:63 registers a window 'storage' listener; the others never rebuild their cache when another tab writes, so a keybinding or view option changed in tab A is silently stale in tab B until reload. Write one createLocalStore(key, parse, fallback) factory in client/src/lib/local-store.ts — cache, subscribe, setState, a storage-event listener, and a hook — and migrate every store onto it, preserving each store's exported API exactly (their one-off behaviors like view-options' legacy per-session blob fold-in and keybindings' diff-from-defaults stay as thin wrappers over the factory). This should delete roughly 400 lines net.

Verify: cd client && pnpm exec tsc -b. Summarize the migration and the net line delta.

steps.name: refactor-client-dedup
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Three deduplication refactors in the client, no behavior change. You own client/src/components/tool-views.tsx, the settings pages listed below, one new hook file, the four menu surfaces listed below, and one new shared descriptor module.

1. tool-views.tsx:1196/:1282/:1296 — toolHasDetail, toolOpensByDefault and ToolDetail are three functions keyed off the same ToolView union whose agreement is enforced only by a comment. Replace with a Record<ToolView, { Detail, opensByDefault, hasDetail }> registry so adding a view is one edit and the union is exhaustiveness-checked.
2. The busy-state + try/catch + error-toast block is copy-pasted across settings/personas.tsx:89, settings/agents.tsx:131 and :180, settings/mcp.tsx:139, settings/quota.tsx:204 and :258, settings/profiles.tsx:246. Add a useAsyncAction() hook returning { busy, run } (run wraps reportError/captureError per the errors.ts conventions in CLAUDE.md — dialogs hold their own errors via captureError, background actions toast) and collapse the seven blocks.
3. Thread action menus are assembled independently in thread-menu.tsx (14 items), item-context-menu.tsx (13), sidebar/thread-row.tsx (10), thread-sidebar.tsx (11) — pin/rename/delete/restore appear in at least three with separately written JSX. Introduce a threadMenuItems(session, actions) descriptor array in a shared module and render it from each surface's own menu primitives, keeping each surface's item subset and ordering exactly as it is today.

Verify: cd client && pnpm exec tsc -b. Summarize each dedup and the net line delta.

phases.name: optimize
phases.description: Performance work that builds on the refactored shapes.

steps.name: optimize-store-selector
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. The highest-value client performance fix. You own client/src/lib/store.tsx and client/src/components/thread-view.tsx, plus mechanical hook swaps in other components.

useStore() (client/src/lib/store.tsx:1376) subscribes ~63 call sites to the whole State. The context split at store.tsx:1341-1350 is already documented as the intended fix but the migration stalled: ThreadView takes the wide hook (thread-view.tsx:269), so a streamed token in ANY background thread produces a new State, re-renders every open transcript (the dock keeps every opened transcript mounted) and re-runs ThreadView's six useMemo derivations. Implement a useThread(sessionId) selector — useSyncExternalStore over the reducer's store with per-thread reference equality, or completing the documented context split, whichever the existing architecture supports more cleanly — and migrate ThreadView and the other transcript-path consumers onto it. Then sweep the remaining wide-hook call sites that only read one thread or one top-level slice and narrow them mechanically. The acceptance test: with two threads open, a streamed update in thread A must not re-render thread B's transcript (verify by reasoning about referential equality through the new selector — no browser automation, per CLAUDE.md).

Verify: cd client && pnpm exec tsc -b. Summarize the mechanism and which call sites were narrowed.

steps.name: optimize-workspace-fs
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Make the server's workspace walk async. You own server/src/workspace-fs.ts and its call sites in server/src/routes/workspace.ts and server/src/mentions.ts if signatures ripple.

server/src/workspace-fs.ts:233,255,265,381 does readdirSync plus one or two statSync per entry on the event loop. This backs GET /api/projects/:id/files (routes/workspace.ts:70) and the file-search route (:83) that the composer's @-mention completer hits per keystroke — on a large repo it blocks every WebSocket fan-out (sessions.ts:740) in the same process that owns every agent child. Convert the walk to fs.promises with bounded concurrency, preserving exactly: DEFAULT_IGNORES, never descending symlinks, the SEARCH_VISIT_LIMIT budget, breadth-first order (the truncation contract — shallow paths are the ones a person meant), the ranking, and the lexical+realpath containment checks. Also fix the minor one-pass items if trivially in reach: project-stats.ts:119-140's three passes over the same array can be one (only if you also own that file cleanly — otherwise leave it and say so).

Verify: cd server && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize the conversion and confirm each preserved invariant.

steps.name: optimize-agent-persistence
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Fix O(history) persistence in the agent package. You own agent/src/persistence.ts and its call sites in agent/src/session.ts / agent/src/app.ts if signatures ripple.

agent/src/persistence.ts:70-73 rewrites the full session index on every touch() — called on each prompt — and read() at :113 slurps the entire JSONL into memory. Both are O(total history) per turn. Make touch() update only the touched entry (an in-memory index flushed debounced, or an append-plus-compact scheme — pick what fits the file's existing design; the index must survive a crash well enough that session/list still answers, which is what makes threads importable per the README). For read(), stream the JSONL line by line instead of slurping; the compact barrier logic (:123) must keep working. Do not change the on-disk format unless unavoidable — other tooling may read ~/.daedalus-agent/; if you must, say so loudly in your final message.

Verify: cd agent && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm test. Summarize the scheme chosen.

phases.name: finish
phases.description: Wiring gaps, dead code, workspace scripts, then a full verification sweep over everything the run changed.

steps.name: cleanup-wiring
steps.prompt:
You are working in the daedalus-harness repo. Close out the audit's loose ends. You own: server/src/registry.ts, client/src/lib/router.tsx, the dead-code files listed below, the three package.json files, and a new root package.json.

1. DAEDALUS_AGENT_PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS is agent-side only: agent/src/env.ts:48 reads it and agent/README.md claims the server fills it from the profile and it is editable in Settings > Agents, but the key appears nowhere in server/src/registry.ts's daedalus env template (~:582). Add it to the seed env template following the existing placeholder conventions (literal 'null' means unset; check how sibling keys are seeded and whether a backfill entry is needed per the seedAgents rules in CLAUDE.md) so the documented off switch exists.
2. client/src/lib/router.tsx:14 still documents a /studio route whose page, lib/templates.ts, settings tab and server module were all deleted — fix the route-table comment to match reality.
3. Prune dead exports, verifying each is truly unreferenced before deleting (grep the whole repo, including server and agent): client/src/lib/workspace/git-api.ts's git* functions, fs-api.ts's unused entries, buffers.ts dirtyPaths, terminals.ts listTerminals, panels.ts panelProject, lib/pins.ts isPinned (if the local-store refactor kept it), schemeById, rampFor, rampContrast, fontDef, priorityRank, isEscape, isUnder, joinPath, dirname, BASE_KEYS; server/src/quota.ts:558 invalidateProfileQuota; drop the export keyword from notifications.ts:34 NOTIFICATIONS_LIMIT. If a symbol turns out referenced, keep it and note why the audit flagged it.
4. Workspace scripts: add a root package.json with scripts that run each package's typecheck and test (plain cd-based scripts are fine; the repo is not currently a pnpm workspace — do NOT convert it to one, just orchestrate), and give client/package.json a test script (tsc -b is acceptable as the test stand-in if no runner exists; say so).

Verify: cd client && pnpm exec tsc -b; cd server && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit; cd agent && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit. Summarize each item's outcome.

steps.name: verify-all
